collection: SAT Reading and Writing: quantitative evidence from tables
note: Original stimuli and fictional data, one question per stimulus. Independent academic review pending.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Integrate a short text with an original table to select supported evidence.
questions.prompt: Which statement from the table best supports Mia’s prediction?
questions.passage:
A team tested three coatings on model roof tiles under a lamp. It measured the temperature rise in each tile after the same exposure. Mia predicts that the light coating will give the smallest temperature rise on both tile materials.

| Tile material | No coating (°C) | Light coat (°C) | Dark coat (°C) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Clay | 12 | 7 | 15 |
| Concrete | 10 | 6 | 13 |
options: The dark coating gave clay a smaller rise than it gave concrete.
Uncoated clay and uncoated concrete warmed by the same amount.
For each material, the light-coated tile had a smaller temperature rise than either of the other tiles.
The light coating gave concrete a smaller rise than it gave clay.
questions.answer: For each material, the light-coated tile had a smaller temperature rise than either of the other tiles.
questions.explanation: The prediction compares finishes within each material. Seven is lower than both 12 and 15 for clay, and six is lower than both 10 and 13 for concrete.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Integrate a short text with an original table to select supported evidence.
questions.prompt: Which finding best supports both parts of the report’s claim?
questions.passage:
A town set up collection points for household batteries. A report claims that after the first month, there was a shift toward the market collection point, even though the total number of batteries collected at the two points did not rise.

| Month | Market | Library |
|---|---:|---:|
| March | 40 | 60 |
| April | 65 | 35 |
options: The library count fell, so the combined count fell by 25.
The market count rose and the library count stayed at 60.
The combined count was 100 in April and the market was below the library that month.
The market count rose from 40 to 65 while the combined count stayed at 100.
questions.answer: The market count rose from 40 to 65 while the combined count stayed at 100.
questions.explanation: The market accounted for more of the same total. Both months add to 100, and the market count rose by 25.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Integrate a short text with an original table to select supported evidence.
questions.prompt: Which comparison best supports the team’s interpretation?
questions.passage:
A team tested whether different seed coatings change the timing of germination in a model trial. Equal groups of 50 seeds were observed on day 3 and day 10. The team argues that the coating mainly changed early germination rather than the number of seeds that had germinated by day 10.

| Treatment | Germinated by day 3 | Germinated by day 10 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Coated | 29 | 42 |
| Uncoated | 12 | 43 |
options: The groups differed by 17 seeds on day 3 but by only one seed on day 10.
Both groups had more germinated seeds by day 10 than by day 3.
Ten-day germination was much higher in the coated group.
The uncoated group led by one seed on both observation days.
questions.answer: The groups differed by 17 seeds on day 3 but by only one seed on day 10.
questions.explanation: The gap was large early and small at the end, as the timing interpretation predicts.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Integrate a short text with an original table to select supported evidence.
questions.prompt: Which choice accurately uses the data to support the planner’s claim?
questions.passage:
A museum offered both guided and self-guided visits on two days. A planner claims that guided tours reached a larger share of visitors on Saturday, even though Friday had more guided visitors in absolute numbers.

| Day | Guided visitors | All visitors |
|---|---:|---:|
| Friday | 32 | 160 |
| Saturday | 24 | 80 |
options: Friday’s larger guided count means Friday also had the larger guided share.
Guided visits accounted for 30% of Saturday visits and 20% of Friday visits, although more people took the tour on Friday.
Saturday’s guided share was 15%, half of Friday’s.
Guided visits accounted for the same share on both days because both guided counts were below 40.
questions.answer: Guided visits accounted for 30% of Saturday visits and 20% of Friday visits, although more people took the tour on Friday.
questions.explanation: Divide each guided count by that day’s total. Saturday has a higher proportion despite its lower guided count.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Integrate a short text with an original table to select supported evidence.
questions.prompt: Which row most directly challenges the class’s initial claim?
questions.passage:
A class put moisture sensors in planters with and without mulch. Its initial claim was that adding mulch was associated with a higher reading in every planter location after two days. The readings are given as percentage soil moisture.

| Location | No mulch (%) | Mulch (%) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Open yard | 19 | 24 |
| Covered porch | 23 | 21 |
| East fence | 18 | 22 |
options: In the open yard, moisture was higher with mulch than without it.
At the east fence, moisture was higher with mulch than without it.
At the covered porch, moisture was lower with mulch than without it.
In the open yard, the no-mulch reading was lower than the porch no-mulch reading.
questions.answer: At the covered porch, moisture was lower with mulch than without it.
questions.explanation: A claim about every location is challenged by one opposite result. On the porch, 21% with mulch is below 23% without mulch.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Integrate a short text with an original table to select supported evidence.
questions.prompt: Which sentence most directly supports both parts of the writer’s claim?
questions.passage:
A bus agency compared its punctuality by route before and after a schedule change. A writer wants to support the claim that performance improved on some routes but remained uneven after the change.

| Route | Before: on time (%) | After: on time (%) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Hillside | 62 | 83 |
| Central | 86 | 87 |
| Lake | 76 | 71 |
options: Central’s rate was 86% before the change and 87% afterward.
Lake reached 83% after the change, matching Hillside.
All three routes improved and ended within one percentage point of each other.
Hillside’s on-time rate rose from 62% to 83%, while post-change rates still ranged from 71% on Lake to 87% on Central.
questions.answer: Hillside’s on-time rate rose from 62% to 83%, while post-change rates still ranged from 71% on Lake to 87% on Central.
questions.explanation: The Hillside comparison demonstrates improvement and the Lake–Central spread demonstrates uneven post-change performance.
